note: Taxonomy Multi-delete Terms is a UI enhancement on core Taxonomy. It alters the taxonomy_overview_terms form to add per-row checkboxes + a Delete button (for users with 'access taxonomy multidelete terms'), then routes to a confirm form (taxonomy_multidelete_terms.delete) that batch-deletes the selected terms via TaxonomyMultideleteBatch::processTerms. No config, no schema, no services, no Drush, configure=null. The only persistent module-defined state is its permission, so the medium case reads back which role holds it; the hard case verifies live state (all terms removed from a vocabulary), which is exactly what the bulk-delete flow produces.

evals.prompt: Which permission does the taxonomy_multidelete_terms module add, and what does granting it do on the taxonomy term overview page?
evals.expected_output: It adds the 'access taxonomy multidelete terms' permission. Users with it get a checkbox on every term row plus a 'Delete' button on the vocabulary term overview page, letting them select and bulk-delete terms.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with taxonomy_multidelete_terms enabled, where do I go to delete several taxonomy terms at once, and what happens after I select terms and click Delete?
evals.expected_output: Go to the vocabulary's term overview / Manage terms page (/admin/structure/taxonomy/manage/<vocabulary>/overview), tick the terms and click Delete. You are taken to a confirmation form that lists the terms (warning children are deleted too), and confirming runs a batch that deletes them.

evals.prompt: When bulk-deleting taxonomy terms with taxonomy_multidelete_terms, what happens to a selected term's child terms?
evals.expected_output: Deleting a term also deletes all of its children (the confirmation form warns of this, and it reflects standard core taxonomy behaviour).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one non-core user role has been granted the taxonomy_multidelete_terms bulk-delete permission. Inspect the live site and give the machine name of that role.
evals.expected_output: The role is tmt_bulk: it holds the 'access taxonomy multidelete terms' permission (e.g. drush role:list, or check user.role.tmt_bulk config / Role::load('tmt_bulk')->hasPermission(...)).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a taxonomy vocabulary with machine name tmt_del that currently contains several terms. Delete every term in the tmt_del vocabulary (the vocabulary itself must remain). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: After the task, the tmt_del vocabulary still exists but has zero terms (e.g. use the bulk 'Delete' flow on /admin/structure/taxonomy/manage/tmt_del/overview, or delete the taxonomy_term entities of vid tmt_del programmatically).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a taxonomy vocabulary with machine name tmt_known. Inspect the live site and state how many taxonomy terms it currently contains.
evals.expected_output: The tmt_known vocabulary contains 7 terms (e.g. an entity query counting taxonomy_term entities with vid tmt_known).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the taxonomy vocabulary tmt_half contains six terms: three whose names begin with 'tmt_keep_' and three whose names begin with 'tmt_del_'. Delete only the three terms whose names begin with 'tmt_del_', leaving the three 'tmt_keep_' terms intact. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: After the task tmt_half has the three tmt_keep_* terms and none of the tmt_del_* terms (e.g. select just those three on the term overview bulk-delete flow, or delete the matching taxonomy_term entities).
